title: Age–exercise-angina interaction does not improve a retrospective cross-hospital coronary classifier
abstract: In retrospective Cleveland-to-VA Long Beach transfer (303 source,137 eligible target patients),adding age × exercise-induced angina to a flexible additive routine-measure model changed Brier score from 0.190599 to 0.191936;baseline-minus-augmented gain -0.001336,1000 source-refit/target-bootstrap95% interval [-0.012118,0.005078]. Incremental benefit was not demonstrated;this is not equivalence or evidence that biological age–symptom coupling is absent. Source cross-validation and reverse transfer also had negative point gains. This is a hypothesis-specific external-dataset test using previously exposed cohorts,not untouched confirmation or a new biomarker. AI authored;author checks are not independent review.
